### Steps to reproduce issue

1. Create a class that inherits from rclcpp::Node and contains another rclcpp::Node internally.

2. Some of the nodes are terminated shortly after startup without performing any additional actions, while the remaining nodes stay idle using spin (they don’t even need to be registered to an executor).

3. Launch 100 instances of this node — 2 nodes terminate immediately, and 98 remain active.

### Expected behavior

All nodes show normal (low) CPU usage because they do almost nothing.

### Actual behavior

<img width="1200" height="600" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d416a4c6-0049-471d-83f5-ab00ea7e1a90" />

Some nodes exhibit abnormal CPU usage, as shown in the graph above.

This phenomenon begins to appear when there are more than 30 nodes, and it almost always occurs when there are 100 or more.

### Additional information

Environments
- Ubuntu 20.04
- foxy
- AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor
- Mem 128G

While developing on the Foxy version, I observed abnormal CPU usage. To reproduce the same issue, we used the following code.


```
// test_node.cpp

#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>

class TestNode : public rclcpp::Node
{
public:
  explicit TestNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions & options = rclcpp::NodeOptions())
  : rclcpp::Node("test_node", options)
  {
    RCLCPP_INFO(get_logger(), "TestNode constructed");
    rclcpp::NodeOptions inner_options = options;
    inner_options.use_global_arguments(false);

    declare_parameter("node_id", 0);
    auto node_id = get_parameter("node_id").get_value<int>();
    RCLCPP_ERROR_STREAM(get_logger(), "echo : " << node_id );
    inner_node_ = std::make_shared<rclcpp::Node>("inner_node" + std::to_string(node_id), inner_options);
  }

private:
  std::shared_ptr<rclcpp::Node> inner_node_;
};

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    rclcpp::init(argc, argv);
    auto node = std::make_shared<TestNode>();
    auto node_id = node->get_parameter("node_id").get_value<int>();
    if (node_id > 1) {
        rclcpp::executors::SingleThreadedExecutor executor;
        executor.spin();
    }
    rclcpp::shutdown();
    return 0;
}

```

Launch file:
```
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node

def generate_launch_description():
    node_count = 100
    package_name = 'node_test'
    executable_name = 'test_node'
    base_node_name = 'test_node'

    nodes = []

    for i in range(node_count):
        node = Node(
            package=package_name,
            executable=executable_name,
            name=f'{base_node_name}_{i:02d}',
            output='screen',
            emulate_tty=True,
            parameters=[
                {'node_id': i},
            ],
        )
        nodes.append(node)

    return LaunchDescription(nodes)

```

I would really appreciate any help or insight on this issue.
Thanks in advance.

Steps to reproduce issue

  1. Create a class that inherits from rclcpp::Node and contains another rclcpp::Node internally.

  2. Some of the nodes are terminated shortly after startup without performing any additional actions, while the remaining nodes stay idle using spin (they don’t even need to be registered to an executor).

  3. Launch 100 instances of this node — 2 nodes terminate immediately, and 98 remain active.

Expected behavior

All nodes show normal (low) CPU usage because they do almost nothing.

Actual behavior

Some nodes exhibit abnormal CPU usage, as shown in the graph above.

This phenomenon begins to appear when there are more than 30 nodes, and it almost always occurs when there are 100 or more.

Additional information

Environments

  • Ubuntu 20.04
  • foxy
  • AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor
  • Mem 128G

While developing on the Foxy version, I observed abnormal CPU usage. To reproduce the same issue, we used the following code.

// test_node.cpp

#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>

class TestNode : public rclcpp::Node
{
public:
  explicit TestNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions & options = rclcpp::NodeOptions())
  : rclcpp::Node("test_node", options)
  {
    RCLCPP_INFO(get_logger(), "TestNode constructed");
    rclcpp::NodeOptions inner_options = options;
    inner_options.use_global_arguments(false);

    declare_parameter("node_id", 0);
    auto node_id = get_parameter("node_id").get_value<int>();
    RCLCPP_ERROR_STREAM(get_logger(), "echo : " << node_id );
    inner_node_ = std::make_shared<rclcpp::Node>("inner_node" + std::to_string(node_id), inner_options);
  }

private:
  std::shared_ptr<rclcpp::Node> inner_node_;
};

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    rclcpp::init(argc, argv);
    auto node = std::make_shared<TestNode>();
    auto node_id = node->get_parameter("node_id").get_value<int>();
    if (node_id > 1) {
        rclcpp::executors::SingleThreadedExecutor executor;
        executor.spin();
    }
    rclcpp::shutdown();
    return 0;
}

Launch file:

from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node

def generate_launch_description():
    node_count = 100
    package_name = 'node_test'
    executable_name = 'test_node'
    base_node_name = 'test_node'

    nodes = []

    for i in range(node_count):
        node = Node(
            package=package_name,
            executable=executable_name,
            name=f'{base_node_name}_{i:02d}',
            output='screen',
            emulate_tty=True,
            parameters=[
                {'node_id': i},
            ],
        )
        nodes.append(node)

    return LaunchDescription(nodes)

I would really appreciate any help or insight on this issue.
Thanks in advance.

Following your advice, I tested the issue in the Humble version (since using newer versions is currently difficult in our environment), and there was a definite improvement — the problem no longer occurs.

That said, we’ll likely need to keep using Foxy for a short period. Could you briefly share your thoughts on what might be causing this issue in Foxy?

I understand that Foxy is already EOL, but I’d like to know whether there’s anything in the current implementation itself that could be problematic.

@sh-park-rf thanks for creating issue.

it is really hard to tell what could be possibly reason for this... foxy just does not have many bug fixes compared to supported distributions. and i think anyone barely takes the effort to this issue because Foxy is E.O.L.

that said, i would recommend that if you have to use Foxy for now. how about switching the RMW implementation to rmw_cyclonedds to see if the problem can be solved? https://docs.ros.org/en/foxy/Installation/DDS-Implementations/Working-with-Eclipse-CycloneDDS.html

comments.body:
@fujitatomoya thank you for your reply!
Following your suggestion, I switched to using rmw_cyclonedds, and the issue has disappeared.
I had been hesitant to use Cyclone DDS because I’d heard it generally has higher latency than Fast DDS, but it seems that, at least for the Foxy version, using Cyclone DDS is unavoidable.
Since this appears to be a low-level issue related to the DDS layer, and it has already been resolved in Humble, I’ll go ahead and close this issue.
Thank you for your help.
